definitions.explanation: The administrative office of a Shinto shrine, where visitors can purchase amulets, charms, and other items, and where shrine administrative work is conducted.

examples.japanese: {社務所|しゃむしょ}でお{守|まも}りを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a charm at the shrine office.

examples.japanese: {御朱印|ごしゅいん}は{社務所|しゃむしょ}でもらえます。
examples.english: You can get a shrine stamp at the shrine office.

examples.japanese: {七五三|しちごさん}の{祈祷|きとう}の{申|もう}し{込|こ}みは{社務所|しゃむしょ}で{受|う}け{付|つ}けている。
examples.english: Applications for Shichi-Go-San prayer ceremonies are accepted at the shrine office.

notes:
A compound of {社|しゃ} (shrine) + {務|む} (duties, affairs) + {所|しょ} (place). The {社務所|しゃむしょ} is typically a building near the main shrine building where priests and staff handle administrative tasks and interact with visitors. It is the place to go for purchasing お{守|まも}り (charms), {御朱印|ごしゅいん} (seal stamps), and arranging prayer ceremonies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社務所|しゃむしょ}でお{守|まも}りを{買|か}う: to buy a charm at the shrine office
- {社務所|しゃむしょ}の{受付|うけつけ}: reception at the shrine office
- {社務所|しゃむしょ}の{営業時間|えいぎょうじかん}: shrine office hours

RELATED TERMS:
- {寺務所|じむしょ}: temple office — the Buddhist temple equivalent
- {神社|じんじゃ}: Shinto shrine — the overall institution
- お{守|まも}り: amulet, charm — commonly purchased at the shrine office
- {御朱印|ごしゅいん}: seal stamp — collected by visitors at the shrine office
